title: Improve trigsimp for hyperbolic functions nested in non-trig functions
description:
#### References to other Issues or PRs
Fixes #19535

#### Brief description of what is fixed or changed
Previously `_futrig` was called via `bottom_up` for "regular" trigonometric functions but not for hyperbolic trigonometric functions. This inhibited some obvious simplifications, e.g. the following stayed unchanged: `trigsimp(sqrt(cosh(x)**2 - 1))`

#### Other comments
This PR also removes unused `**kwargs` in `_futrig`.

#### Release Notes

<!-- Write the release notes for this release below. See
https://github.com/sympy/sympy/wiki/Writing-Release-Notes for more information
on how to write release notes. The bot will check your release notes
automatically to see if they are formatted correctly. -->

<!-- BEGIN RELEASE NOTES -->
* simplify
  * Improved `trigsimp` for hyperbolic functions nested in non-trig functions.
<!-- END RELEASE NOTES -->

> The doc should be rewritten perhaps with an example for which zero-testing is impossible:

(And the other 2 doctests concerning that example have already been disabled even before this PR...)

review_comments.author: eric-wieser
review_comments.body:
This results in a worse simplification when
This results in a worse simplification when
```python
e = -t*sin(_Dummy*alpha/2)**2 + t*cos(_Dummy*alpha/2)**2 - 2*I*x*sin(_Dummy*alpha/2)*cos(_Dummy*alpha/2)
```
(`_Dummy` inserted by `hyper_as_trig`). The results are
```python
ipdb> _futrig(e)
t*cos(_Dummy*alpha) - I*x*sin(_Dummy*alpha)
ipdb> bottom_up(e, _futrig)
-2*t*sin(_Dummy*alpha/2)**2 + t - I*x*sin(_Dummy*alpha)
```
See #19917 for a full repro
